standard_prerequisites.use: Morphisms-chapter facts that a universal homeomorphism is submersive with universally injective underlying map and that a flat closed immersion is an open-and-closed immersion/isomorphism on components; Schemes, lemma monomorphism (diagonal iso iff monomorphism); Descent, lemma flat-surjective-quasi-compact-monomorphism-isomorphism.

core_obligations: Prove the diagonal is a surjective closed immersion.
Kill it with flatness to get a monomorphism.
Conclude via the fpqc monomorphism-isomorphism criterion.

proof_roadmap.step: Diagonal analysis of a universal homeomorphism.
Flat closed immersion rigidity plus descent of isomorphisms along qc monomorphisms.

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the scheme-theoretic generalization (the author flags it as such, subsumption of the field-theoretic fact that a separable purely inseparable extension is trivial) stating that a morphism which is both weakly etale and a universal homeomorphism is an isomorphism. The retained proof is written: the diagonal of a universal homeomorphism is a surjective closed immersion (cited Morphisms lemmas homeomorphism-affine and universally-injective), a closed immersion that is also flat is an isomorphism (cited Morphisms lemma characterize-flat-closed-immersions), so the diagonal is an isomorphism, i.e. f is a monomorphism (Schemes, lemma monomorphism); f is quasi-compact as a universal homeomorphism, and a flat surjective quasi-compact monomorphism is an isomorphism by the cited Descent lemma. Every step names its input. Retained author proof at lines 19195-19208.

dedup.scope: Rigidity statement: weakly etale + universal homeomorphism forces isomorphism.
